correctness.rationale: For the six-coefficient real polynomial jerk with b4!=0, direct differentiation gives dot P=b4*x^2+(b5-b8)*y^2. When b4*(b5-b8)>=0, sP is nondecreasing for s=sign(b4). Bounded forward orbits have compact invariant omega-limits where P is constant and x must vanish identically, forcing y=z=0 by the original differential equations. Two-sided bounded orbits also have trivial alpha-limit, and monotonicity eliminates nonconstant such orbits. For compact invariant measures, integrating the generator identity and invariance gives the unique equilibrium mass on the closed cone or the stated exact second-moment ratio in the opposite cone. When b4*(b5-b8)<0, the coefficient choices b2=b4/(b5-b8), b3=b5=b7=0, b8=-(b5-b8) make z=-omega^2*x invariant and yield harmonic cycles for every amplitude. The attached CHECK.py executes exact symbolic assertions for P, oscillator solutions and all nine published table signs. No numerical experiment supplies an infinite-time proof.

value.rationale: The 2015 six-coefficient jerk classification illustrates nine numerical chaotic regimes with a unique nonhyperbolic equilibrium but provides no exact global parameter barrier for compact recurrence. The theorem gives a closed sharp sign cone valid independently of the other four coefficients, proves convergence of every bounded forward orbit on that cone, excludes every nontrivial compact full invariant set, and classifies its stationary probabilities. For each opposite-sign coefficient pair it gives an explicit continuum of harmonic periodic witnesses, proving coefficient-uniform sharpness; outside the cone it fixes an exact mean-square ratio for invariant measures, providing an objective check on chaotic simulations. This parameter-sharp family-level dynamical dichotomy is mathematically motivated by the published search for chaotic coefficient regimes, not an arbitrary slice or merely an algebraic identity. It does not claim existence of chaos or all-orbit boundedness.
